scenes.headline: show()
scenes.subtitle: Previewing rows during development.
scenes.narration: The show action prints a formatted preview of a DataFrame's rows to the console, and it triggers execution.

scenes.headline: What show does
items: Prints rows as a neat table to the console
Is an action, so it runs the whole plan
Great for debugging, not for capturing results
scenes.narration: Show prints rows as a neat console table and defaults to the first twenty. Because it is an action it executes the entire plan up to that point, making it perfect for debugging though not for capturing results in code.

scenes.headline: Previewing with show
scenes.code:
logs_df.show(5, truncate=False)
# 5 rows, full column values, no truncation
scenes.narration: Here we ask show for the first five rows and set truncate to false so long column values are printed in full rather than cut off. This is the fastest way to sanity-check what your transformations actually produced.

scenes.text: show is for humans reading a console — use collect or write to capture data in code.
scenes.narration: Remember that show is meant for a human reading the console; to capture data in code you use collect or write instead.
